Users must explicitly ask to show the hidden files either via a series of Graphical User Interface (GUI) prompts or with command line switches (dir /a for Windows and ls –a for Linux and macOS).

If you ever suspect an email to be a phishing attack, please follow our procedures for reporting it immediately.
For years, spear phishers have used file attachments to spread malicious software (malware) through email messages.

These attachments contain malicious files, such as keystroke loggers that allow them to steal your credentials, or Trojan horses to have access to your network; your computer is vulnerable as soon as you download the attachment.
Identifying dangerous attachments can be quite difficult, even for the experts. However, there are things that will help you identify a fraudulent email.
The attachment is out of context: For instance, you receive a file named "Payroll," and you work in Fulfillment.
The type of file attached is not related to the subject of the email: For example, you are asked to review a document, but the file extension is an executable file (.exe).

The file extension appears to contain two file types: If you receive a file called "wiring_process.pdf.exe," for example, the sender might be trying to make the file appear more innocent upon a first glance.

Additionally, spear phishers can place the malicious attachment inside a compressed folder (.zip file) to make it appear more innocent. Password-protected .zip files have a higher chance of making it past your spam filters and into your inbox.
Other common file types are Word documents, PDFs, or Java.class files. Such files are easy to embed unseen code into, and downloading a malicious file can compromise the security of your computer.

Make sure the file extension matches the function of the file. If you think you're downloading an MP3 Audio file, but the extension is .exe, don't download it. Often, once the file's on your computer, the damage is already done.
If you suspect that you have received a spear phishing email at work follow our procedures for reporting it immediately.
